Fibra Prologis stock narrows 2026 outlook as occupancy eases
sum: FIBRA Prologis reported its third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, October 21, with occupancy easing from a year earlier while rent growth remained strong. In its earnings release, the Mexican industrial real estate trust said net effective rents on rollover rose 36.2 percent and funds from operations per CBFI reached 0.0574 dollars.

Period-end occupancy was 96.5 percent, compared with 98.0 percent in the third quarter of 2025. Average occupancy stood at 95.1 percent, while customer retention declined to 66.0 percent from 81.7 percent.

Leases commenced during the quarter covered 2.9 million square feet, down from 4.1 million square feet a year earlier. Same-store cash net operating income rose 1.7 percent, compared with 14.8 percent in the prior-year quarter.

FIBRA Prologis set its 2026 year-end occupancy outlook at 96.5 to 97.5 percent and its same-store cash NOI growth forecast at 7.0 to 8.0 percent. The trust also set building acquisitions at 100 million dollars and maintained its full-year distribution guidance at 0.1700 dollars per CBFI.

As of September 30, leverage was 24.2 percent and liquidity was approximately 1.2 billion dollars, including 1.0 billion dollars of available unsecured credit capacity and 167 million dollars of unrestricted cash. Management said improving customer demand and lower construction starts were encouraging signs, while the portfolio's rent mark-to-market offered potential support as market conditions improve.

FIBRA Prologis owns and operates Class-A industrial real estate in Mexico, with logistics and manufacturing facilities across six core markets. As of September 30, its portfolio comprised 515 investment properties totaling 87.3 million square feet. SiiLA identified FIBRA Prologis as the largest industrial owner in its analyzed Mexican market, ahead of FIBRA Uno, FIBRA Monterrey and Vesta by portfolio share, while noting that no owner dominated the national market.

items.t: Prologis Inc. stock gains as investors digest $19 billion SEGRO deal and valuation debate
sum: Prologis Inc. stock (ISIN US74340W1036) is trading around USD 135 on the New York Stock Exchange as of September 11, 2026, leaving investors to weigh the impact of the company’s planned USD 19 billion acquisition of UK warehouse operator SEGRO and the resulting valuation debate.

According to Simply Wall St on September 11, 2026, Prologis has agreed a USD 19 billion transaction to acquire SEGRO, significantly expanding its European logistics footprint and data-center exposure.

As AINvest reports, Prologis funded part of the cash consideration by issuing roughly 15 million new shares in a public offering that raised about USD 2.1 billion at an offer price of USD 140 per share, with the stock closing that day down about 2.8 percent at the offering level.

The same analysis notes that, at about USD 134 per share, Prologis is trading near 22 times the midpoint of this year’s core funds-from-operations (FFO) guidance, implying a premium valuation relative to some industrial real estate peers and highlighting how much future growth from the SEGRO and data-center strategy is already priced in.AINvest

In its September 11, 2026 note, Simply Wall St estimates a fair value of about USD 128 per Prologis share, which it states is roughly 5.2 percent below the recent market price, implying that the stock could be modestly overvalued following the SEGRO announcement.

The implied comparison is clear: if investors accept a fair value of USD 128 while the shares change hands near USD 135, the premium is around USD 7 per share, or a bit more than 5 percent, suggesting that expectations for future rental growth and development returns are elevated.

For investors, the key question now is whether incremental earnings from SEGRO’s portfolio and a pivot toward data-center assets will be sufficient to grow core FFO enough to justify paying roughly 22 times the midpoint of this year’s guidance, as highlighted by AINvest.

Prologis to acquire SEGRO in £14bn deal at 39% premium
sum: Prologis Inc agrees to acquire SEGRO plc in a £14.0 billion deal, expanding its European footprint by 47% and creating a combined portfolio of 368 million square feet. The transaction offers SEGRO shareholders 0.0920 new Prologis shares per share, with a partial cash alternative capped at £3.5 billion.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Prologis Inc has agreed to acquire UK-based logistics real estate company SEGRO plc in a recommended transaction valued at approximately £14.0 billion. Announced on Aug. 4, 2026, the deal marks a significant expansion of Prologis' European platform, combining the two companies' portfolios into a global entity with approximately £200 billion of assets under management. The acquisition strengthens Prologis' position in the European logistics market, creating an operating portfolio of 368 million square feet and expanding its European footprint by 47%. For shareholders, the move aims to enhance long-term earnings potential while maintaining credit ratings.

The transaction structure involves SEGRO shareholders receiving 0.0920 new Prologis shares for each SEGRO share held. Shareholders may elect to receive cash in lieu of some or all of their Prologis share consideration under a partial cash alternative. The maximum aggregate amount of cash available under this alternative is approximately £3,509,777,110.70. Each shareholder's basic entitlement under the partial cash alternative equals 25% of the fixed price of 1,031.7 pence per SEGRO share, translating to 258 pence in cash and 0.0690 new Prologis shares for each SEGRO share if only the basic entitlement is elected. Elections exceeding the basic entitlement will be scaled back pro rata if total requests exceed the maximum cash amount.

SEGRO shareholders will also be entitled to receive and retain any 2026 interim dividend of up to 10.14 pence per share and any 2026 final dividend of up to 22.56 pence per share, which SEGRO intends to pay prior to closing. The cash consideration payable under the partial cash alternative will be funded through a committed term loan facility entered into on Aug. 4, 2026, existing liquidity, and other available sources of funding.

items.t: Prologis Strikes Deal to Acquire Segro in £14.3 Billion Logistics Property Merger
sum: Prologis (NYSE:PLD) has reached an agreement to acquire Segro Plc (LSE:SGRO) in a transaction worth approximately £14.3 billion, combining two of the world's largest industrial property owners. Once completed, the enlarged business will oversee around $269 billion of logistics real estate assets, significantly increasing Prologis' scale across Europe.

The agreed offer values Segro at 1,031.7 pence per share, with investors receiving 0.0920 newly issued Prologis shares for each Segro share they own. The offer represents a 14.4% premium to Segro's most recently reported net asset value of 902 pence per share.
Including the proposed 2026 final dividend of up to 22.56 pence per share, the overall value rises to 1,054.3 pence per share.

As an alternative, shareholders may elect to receive part of their consideration in cash. Up to £3.5 billion has been allocated for the cash option, representing one quarter of the total transaction value. Those selecting the standard mixed consideration will receive 258 pence in cash alongside 0.0690 Prologis shares for each Segro share held. If requests exceed the available cash pool, allocations will be reduced proportionally. Prologis said the cash component will be financed through committed borrowing facilities and existing cash resources.

The acquisition will substantially strengthen Prologis' position in Europe by adding Segro's extensive warehouse portfolio. Together, the combined group will manage approximately 368 million square feet of logistics space across the continent.

The merger will also expand Prologis' European development pipeline to around 13 million square feet while more than doubling its regional land bank, providing significant capacity for future projects.

"This deal brings together SEGRO's exceptional portfolio and customer relationships with Prologis' global platform, operating expertise and financial strength," Prologis Chief Executive Daniel S. Letter said.

THIS IS AN ANNOUNCEMENT FALLING UNDER RULE 2.4 OF THE CITY CODE ON TAKEOVERS AND MERGERS (THE "CODE") AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A FIRM INTENTION TO MAKE AN OFFER UNDER RULE 2.7 OF THE CODE. THERE CAN BE NO CERTAINTY THAT ANY FIRM OFFER WILL BE MADE.

Following submission of our latest proposal, senior representatives of Prologis, Inc. ("Prologis") met with SEGRO plc ("SEGRO") management in London on Sunday. Having submitted a revised proposal only days earlier, the purpose of that meeting was not to present a further revised offer, but rather to understand whether there was a credible path to a transaction capable of recommendation by the SEGRO Board.
We were disappointed that the discussion did not provide meaningful clarity regarding the matters that would enable further progress.

Prologis is very active across the real estate markets in Europe. Prologis' assessment of SEGRO's value is grounded in the quality of its real estate and our expectations for its long-term performance. SEGRO's total property portfolio as at 31 December 2025 was valued at £19.0 billion. Of this, £16.7 billion was categorised as completed assets at an EPRA Net Initial Yield of 4.2 per cent. At market close on 20 July 2026 the UK 10-year Gilt had risen to 5.04 per cent.

In SEGRO's Trading Update published on 8 July 2026, it outlined that NAV had declined from 925 pence per share to 905 pence per share over the six months to 30 June 2026. The NAV reflects SEGRO's independent valuers' assessment of the value of all development land and property assets owned by SEGRO as at 30 June 2026. It is very unusual for a real estate defence document to publish a declining NAV during an offer period.
SEGRO has consistently traded at a significant discount to its EPRA NTA.

sum: Prologis PLD is slated to report its second-quarter 2026 results on July 16, before the opening bell. In anticipation of the announcement, industry analysts and investors are eager to assess the company's performance and prospects in the current economic climate.

In the last reported quarter, this leading industrial REIT posted core funds from operations (FFO) per share of $1.50, up 5.6% from a year ago. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.49%. Results were supported by robust leasing activity.

Over the trailing four quarters, Prologis beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate for FFO per share on three occasions and met in the remaining period, with the average beat being 2.09%. This is depicted in the graph below:

The U.S. industrial real estate market strengthened further in the second quarter of 2026. According to a Cushman & Wakefield report, national vacancy declined to 6.9%, suggesting the market has moved beyond its cyclical peak. Net absorption increased 21% from the prior quarter to 62.1 million square feet, bringing first-half demand to 113.6 million square feet — the strongest first-half performance since 2023.

Occupiers continue to favor buildings with higher clear heights, stronger power capacity and infrastructure suited for automation and AI systems. Dallas–Fort Worth, Phoenix, Atlanta and several Midwest logistics hubs performed well, while port markets, including Houston, New Jersey, Los Angeles and Savannah, GA, also posted healthy demand.

Leasing activity accelerated despite longer transaction timelines. Year-to-date leasing reached a four-year high, up 16% from a year earlier, with Dallas–Fort Worth, the Inland Empire and Chicago leading the country. Third-party logistics companies and manufacturers accounted for more than 55% of leasing volume as businesses expanded and adjusted their supply chains.

Supply remained relatively controlled. Second-quarter deliveries totaled 62 million square feet, down 16% year over year, while first-half completions were 19.2% below the same period in 2025. At the same time, the construction pipeline increased to 305.1 million square feet, up 18% from a year earlier. More than one-third of the pipeline is build-to-suit, reducing the risk of excessive speculative supply.
